title: Evaluation and restriction of extension from the small to the big etale site
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and use compatible small site presentations in the universe convention [def-weil-size-convention]. Write $B_S=(\mathrm{Sch}/S)_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and $\pi_S:\mathrm{Sh}(B_S)\to\mathrm{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{Et}})$ for the big-to-small geometric morphism of [lem-trf-big-small-etale-exact-retraction]. For a morphism of schemes $a:T\to S$, write $a_s:\mathrm{Sh}(T_{\mathrm{Et}})\to\mathrm{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{Et}})$ for the small etale morphism induced by base change, with inverse images and sections as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology]. For every abelian sheaf $F$ on $S_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] there is a canonical isomorphism of abelian groups
$$(\pi_S^{-1}F)(T\xrightarrow{a}S)\cong\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{Et}},a_s^{-1}F).$$
It is natural in $F$ and in $T/S$: if $h:T'\to T$ is over $S$, its restriction map is pullback of sections along $h_s$, using $(a\circ h)_s^{-1}F\cong h_s^{-1}a_s^{-1}F$. Moreover, for any $f:X\to Y$, if $f_b^{-1}$ is restriction from $B_Y$ to $B_X$, then there is a natural isomorphism of abelian sheaves
$$f_b^{-1}\pi_Y^{-1}F\cong\pi_X^{-1}f_s^{-1}F.$$
Here restriction sends $H$ to $(T\to X)\mapsto H(T\to X\to Y)$.

source.place: Tag 09XN, lemma-describe-pullback, evaluation formula and its first proof paragraph; topologies.tex Tag 021I, lemma-morphism-big-small-etale (3), the commutative small/big square.

proof.text: Work in the compatible small presentations of [def-weil-size-convention]. For $f:X\to Y$, identify $B_X$ with $B_Y/(X/Y)$: an object is a scheme over $X$, and the coverings on either side are the same jointly surjective etale families. This is the localized topology of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Put $u_f(V/X)=(V/Y)$ and $v_f(W/Y)=(W\times_YX/X)$, using [def-pc-fibre-product]. Write $P_fG=G\circ u_f$ and $Q_fH=H\circ v_f$ for abelian sheaves. The former is a sheaf by restriction to the localized site. The latter is a sheaf too: a covering $\{W_i\to W\}$ in $B_Y$ pulls back along $W\times_YX\to W$ to the covering $\{W_i\times_YX\to W\times_YX\}$ by the site axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](1); its overlaps are the corresponding fibre products by their universal property. Thus its sheaf equalizer is precisely that of $H$ on this covering. These formulas also specify the functors on arrows.

source.place: Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; the localization definition and restriction formula of Tag 00Y0, definition-localize

proof.text: The adjunction $P_f\dashv Q_f$ can be constructed explicitly. Let $p_W:u_fv_fW\to W$ be the first projection and $e_V:V\to v_fu_fV$ the graph $(\mathrm{id}_V,V\to X)$. For $\alpha:P_fG\to H$, set $\lambda(\alpha)_W=\alpha_{v_fW}\circ G(p_W)$; for $\gamma:G\to Q_fH$, set $\mu(\gamma)_V=H(e_V)\circ\gamma_{u_fV}$. These are natural transformations and homomorphisms since the projections and graphs are natural and all their components are homomorphisms. Naturality of $\alpha$ gives $\mu\lambda(\alpha)_V=\alpha_V\circ G(p_{u_fV}\circ u_f(e_V))=\alpha_V$. Naturality of $\gamma$ gives $\lambda\mu(\gamma)_W=H(v_f(p_W)\circ e_{v_fW})\circ\gamma_W=\gamma_W$. Both projection identities follow by comparing the two projections in [def-pc-fibre-product]. The formulas commute with precomposition in $G$ and postcomposition in $H$, so [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-of-natural-bijection] supplies the adjunction. Its unit $b_{f,G}:G\to Q_fP_fG$ has component $G(p_W)$, by taking $\alpha=\mathrm{id}$. In particular $P_f=f_b^{-1}$ is the restriction in the statement, and $Q_f$ is its right adjoint. Composition of these restrictions is literally composition of the structure maps.

source.place: Tag 021H, lemma-morphism-big-etale, and Sites Tag 03CE, lemma-localize-given-products; explicit Hom bijections and unit

proof.text:
Write $L_Z=\pi_Z^{-1}$ and $R_Z=\pi_{Z,*}$, with unit $e_Z:\mathrm{id}\to R_ZL_Z$. By [lem-trf-big-small-etale-exact-retraction], $R_Z$ is restriction and $e_Z$ is an isomorphism. For an abelian sheaf $H$ on $B_X$ and an etale object $W/Y$, the formulas of step 2 and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] give
$$ (R_YQ_fH)(W/Y)=H(W\times_YX/X)=(f_{s,*}R_XH)(W/Y). $$
On a $Y$-morphism $W'\to W$, both restrictions are $H$ applied to $W'\times_YX\to W\times_YX$, and on a sheaf map both sides use its component there. Hence this is a natural identification $\delta_f:f_{s,*}R_X\xrightarrow{\sim}R_YQ_f$, the identity with common choices of fibre products. This proves the direct-image square of Topologies 021I(3).

source.place: Tag 021I, lemma-morphism-big-small-etale (3), proof: the two composites are the same base-change functor followed by inclusion

proof.text:
The composite adjunctions of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] are $P_fL_Y\dashv R_YQ_f$ and $L_Xf_s^{-1}\dashv f_{s,*}R_X$; the small adjunction is the one of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] to $\delta_f$ from step 3. It gives a canonical natural isomorphism
$$ \beta_f:P_fL_Y\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Xf_s^{-1}. $$
This proves the final clause of the item. More precisely, write $s_{f,F}:F\to f_{s,*}f_s^{-1}F$ for the small unit and $b_f$ for the big unit of step 2. The characterizing equation, with $\delta_f$ understood, is
$$ R_YQ_f(\beta_{f,F})\circ R_Y(b_{f,L_YF})\circ e_{Y,F}
 = f_{s,*}(e_{X,f_s^{-1}F})\circ s_{f,F}. \tag{*} $$
All units here are the abelian adjunction units, so the equation is one of morphisms of abelian sheaves, not merely a bijection of underlying sets.

source.place: Tag 0B65, lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints, and its Hom-set characterization; Tag 0DV0, lemma-compose-counits, composite adjunction

proof.text:
Record the composition compatibility needed for sections. For $a:T\to S$ and $h:T'\to T$, let $c_{a,h}:h_s^{-1}a_s^{-1}\xrightarrow{\sim}(ah)_s^{-1}$ be the unit-compatible comparison of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition](2). Then
$$ \beta_{ah,F}=L_{T'}(c_{a,h,F})\circ\beta_{h,a_s^{-1}F}\circ P_h(\beta_{a,F}), \tag{**} $$
where $P_hP_a=P_{ah}$. To check this, use the composite-unit formula of [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] to expand the unit on the right, substitute $(*)$ first for $h$ and then for $a$, and use the displayed unit equation for $c_{a,h}$ in clause (2) of the cited node. The resulting right-adjoint comparison at $W/S$ is induced by $(W\times_ST)\times_TT'\cong W\times_ST'$, exactly the comparison for $ah$: both maps have the same projections to $W$ and $T'$ by [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus both sides satisfy the same characterizing unit equation for these right adjoints. Uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] gives $(**)$.

source.place: Tag 021J, lemma-composition-etale; Categories Tag 0B65 and Sites Tag 03CB for the unit-compatible inverse-image comparison

proof.text:
For $a:T\to S$ set $K=a_s^{-1}F$. Apply $R_T$ to $\beta_{a,F}:P_aL_SF\cong L_TK$ and compose with $e_{T,K}^{-1}$, which exists by [lem-trf-big-small-etale-exact-retraction]. Evaluating at the final object $T/T$ gives
$$ \theta_{a,F}=(e_{T,K}(T))^{-1}\circ\beta_{a,F}(T):
(L_SF)(T/S)\xrightarrow{\sim}K(T/T)=\Gamma(T_{\mathrm{Et}},a_s^{-1}F). $$
Here $R_TP_aL_SF(T/T)=(L_SF)(T/S)$ by restriction, and $\Gamma$ is evaluation as in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](2). Every map is an abelian-sheaf morphism, so this is an isomorphism of abelian groups. Naturality in $F$ follows from naturality of $\beta_a$ and of $e_T$. This is exactly the evaluation argument in the first paragraph of 09XN: restriction along $T_{\mathrm{Et}}\to B_S$ is $R_TP_a$.

For any abelian sheaf $K$ on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$, evaluate $(*)$ for $h:T'\to T$ at the final object $T/T$. By step 2, $b_{h,L_TK}(T)$ is restriction along $h$, after the canonical identification $T\times_TT'\cong T'$; this identification and its projections are supplied by [def-pc-fibre-product]. The identification $\delta_h$ is the identity of sections from step 3. Thus for $t\in K(T)$ one obtains the actual equality
$$ \beta_{h,K}(T')\big((L_TK)(h)(e_{T,K}(T)t)\big)
 = e_{T',h_s^{-1}K}(T')\big(s_{h,K}(T)t\big). \tag{***} $$
The map $s_{h,K}(T):K(T)\to(h_s^{-1}K)(T')$ is precisely pullback of global sections: by [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](3), it is the inverse-image adjunction unit evaluated at the final object, with direct-image evaluation given by [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. Equation $(***)$ therefore identifies the big restriction with this specific pullback map, including its unit normalization.

source.place: Tag 09XN, lemma-describe-pullback, first proof paragraph, with the adjunction-unit compatibility made explicit; Topologies 021I(3)

proof.text:
Finally let $G=L_SF$, $K=a_s^{-1}F$, $s\in G(T/S)$ and $t=\theta_{a,F}(s)$. By definition $\beta_{a,F}(T)s=e_{T,K}(T)t$. Naturality of the sheaf map $\beta_{a,F}$ along $h:T'\to T$, regarded as an arrow of $B_T$, gives
$$ \beta_{a,F}(T')G(h)s=(L_TK)(h)e_{T,K}(T)t. $$
Apply $\beta_{h,K}(T')$ and use $(***)$, then $(**)$ and the naturality of $e_{T'}$ with respect to $c_{a,h,F}$. Cancelling the isomorphism $e_{T',(ah)_s^{-1}F}(T')$ gives
$$ \theta_{ah,F}(G(h)s)=c_{a,h,F}(T')\big(s_{h,K}(T)t\big). $$
The right side is pullback of $t$ along $h_s$ followed by the canonical identification $h_s^{-1}a_s^{-1}F\cong(ah)_s^{-1}F$ of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition]. This proves exactly the claimed restriction formula and hence naturality in every $T/S$, without any etaleness assumption on $a$ or $h$.
